notes: No amp+cab block — running into tube amp. Amp voicing compensated via Parametric EQ. Delays are tempo-synced to 118 BPM. Three snapshots: rhythm, chorus, and bridge solo. Key tonal difference from other Strokes presets: Hedgehog D9 (Maxon SD9) replaces Stupor OD — harder clipping, more aggressive character matching the song's upbeat, energetic character. 70s Chorus (Boss CE-2 approximation) active on rhythm and chorus snapshots — gives the New Order-adjacent character noted by reviewers.

noise_gate.notes: Tighter gate than Selfless — Hedgehog D9 is harder-clipping than Stupor OD and generates more noise between notes.

compressor.notes: Confirmed on Hammond's board. Provides the consistent, slightly squashed dynamics central to the Strokes' compressed, even-attack rhythm character. ACTIVE in all three snapshots at the same settings — compression is a constant tonal foundation. Mix at 70% blends compressed and dry signal to maintain some pick attack transient.

distortion.notes: Valensi's confirmed Maxon DS830 Distortion Master is closely related to the SD9 circuit. Harder clipping than the Stupor OD used in other Strokes presets — gives Bad Decisions its more energetic, driving character. ACTIVE in all three snapshots.

boost.notes: Nick Valensi confirmed Klon user per YAML. BYPASSED in Snapshots 1 and 2. ACTIVE in Snapshot 3 only for bridge solo — Bright switched On for the glam rock character of the solo.

chorus.notes: Boss CE-2 confirmed on Valensi's board — CE-1 is the closest Helix model. Gives the New Order-adjacent character noted by reviewers. ACTIVE in Snapshots 1 and 2. BYPASSED in Snapshot 3 — bridge solo should be direct and unmodulated. Note: 70s Chorus has separate Chorus and Vibrato rate parameters. Mode set to Chorus to keep dry signal intact.

eq.notes: Snapshots 1 and 2 use telephone filter character — low and high cuts with boosted mids. Snapshot 3 opens up significantly for the bridge solo: wider mid Q, higher mid frequency, open high end. This is the key EQ difference separating solo from rhythm tones.

delay.notes: Delays are tempo-synced to 118 BPM. Snapshots 1 and 2: eighth note (254ms) — tight, driving, matches energetic rhythm character. Snapshot 3: dotted eighth (381ms) — more spacious for bridge solo. Snapshot 3 uses BBD Size 4096 and slight modulation (Rate 2.0Hz, Depth 15%) for a slightly organic vintage delay character appropriate for the glam rock bridge.

reverb.notes: Rhythm snapshots are relatively dry — Bad Decisions has a tight, punchy character. Snapshot 3 opens up for the sustaining bridge solo notes.

1_rhythm.description: Main rhythm/verse tone. Hedgehog D9 at Gain 6.0. Minotaur bypassed. 70s Chorus active at Mix 35% — the New Order-adjacent chorus character. Telephone filter EQ. Tight eighth note delay.

2_chorus.description: Chorus sections. Hedgehog D9 pushed to Gain 7.0, Level 7.0. 70s Chorus still active but Mix pulled to 30%. Tighter delay mix, driest reverb — very punchy and driving.

3_bridge_solo.description: Bridge solo. Hedgehog D9 at maximum Gain 8.5 for high sustain. Minotaur active — Gain 3.0, Tone 5.5, Level 8.5. 70s Chorus bypassed. EQ opens up — Mid at 1.2kHz, High Cut 10kHz, High Gain 0dB. Dotted eighth delay with slight modulation. More reverb for sustaining notes.

playing_notes.pickup_notes: Bridge pickup throughout all three snapshots — this song calls for maximum brightness and attack.
playing_notes.technique: More aggressively strummed than Selfless. Pick firmly and let the Hedgehog D9's harder clipping character compress the strums naturally.
playing_notes.snapshot_cues: Snapshot 1 for verse rhythm. Snapshot 2 for chorus sections. Snapshot 3 for the bridge solo — Hedgehog at max gain plus Minotaur boost gives the high sustain needed for the glam rock solo character described by reviewers.
playing_notes.tone_control: The chorus (Snapshot 2) is the most driving section — resist switching to Snapshot 3 until you reach the bridge solo specifically.
playing_notes.reference: Reviewers described the main guitar riff as worthy of peak-era New Order — the 70s Chorus at Mix 35% in Snapshot 1 is the primary contributor to this character.
